prompt: Redraw this scene as a new, original piece in the same pixel-art style. A home workspace in three-quarter view: a wooden desk under a tall window, an open laptop showing a dark terminal with a few lines of abstract, unreadable code and a small burnt-orange cursor, a ceramic mug, a potted plant with trailing leaves, a pair of headphones, an articulated desk lamp switched off, and, open beside the laptop, a sketchbook with a hand-drawn plan of a small homestead: little squares for buildings, garden rows, a path. Through the window, a small homestead in late-morning daylight: a timber barn, a farmhouse with a stone chimney, tidy garden rows, a split-rail fence, a few fruit trees, a dirt path, and soft green hills beyond. The whole scene fits inside the frame: the desk legs and the chair are fully visible, standing on a few floorboards and a small woven rug, so the vignette has a natural bottom edge. Isolated vignette on a transparent background with nothing outside it. Pixel art with the polish of a lovingly hand-made indie game: drawn on a native canvas of 384 by 256 art pixels, every art pixel exactly 4 by 4 screen pixels on one strict, even grid, no anti-aliasing, no blur, no gradients. One-art-pixel dark outlines that are consistent everywhere, hand-placed dithering only in shadows, readable silhouettes, and a small cohesive palette of about 24 warm colors. Small lived-in details reward a second look. Palette: warm cream (#F4EFE6), paper white (#FFFCF6), near-black ink (#1C1A17), warm greys (#6E665B, #DDD5C7), honey wood, sage and leaf greens, barn red-brown, and a single burnt-orange accent (#B84A16) on the cursor and one or two small details. Calm, warm, hopeful. No people, no animals, no text or letters anywhere, no logos, no user interface, no robots, no glowing brains, no sparkles, no stars.
